A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QVGen, and their supplied pages are readable. However, v1 ends at the references despite referring to an appendix containing proofs, settings, ablations and qualitative results. v3 includes Appendices A–L. Main-text comparisons are reliable, but the missing v1 appendix limits judgments about supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments on four video diffusion models, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, training analyses and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports image-generation results, further analyses and quantization combined with sparse-attention acceleration.

M1.justification: The proposed QVGen procedure retains knowledge-distillation QAT, residual-initialized auxiliary modules, repeated SVD and cosine rank decay, with initial rank 32 and shrinking ratio 1/2. Algorithm 1 expands its documentation. Alternative initializations and decay rules are studied as ablations rather than adopted changes to the default method.

E1.justification: v1 explicitly leaves image generation to future work. v3 adds SD3-medium image experiments: LAION-5B images for the gradient-norm study in G.1, and MJHQ-30K and GenEval evaluation in K. This substantially extends coverage beyond video generation. The original four video models and VBench/VBench-2.0 evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains its comparator set. SVG, previously only cited, becomes a measured comparator in Figure 6(c). Table L also reports Q-DM and EfficientDM in the 5B-model comparison, whereas v1 Table 2 compares only QVGen with full precision. Table L's inconsistent numerical attribution limits the reliability of that added comparison.

E3.justification: The shared main experiments retain their stated settings. v3 reports additional evaluation designs: W6A6 quantization, motion-controlled 8K-video training subsets, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS against BF16 outputs, image evaluation using FID/CLIP/GenEval, and SVG acceleration conditions. These substantially broaden the protocol. Additional settings disclosed for retained experiments do not establish that those experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: The shared component, shrinking-ratio, initial-rank and decay-strategy ablations remain unchanged. v3 G and J provide motion and image/video gradient analyses, annealing and initialization tests, a no-decay control, and random/largest-component decay comparisons. However, v1 explicitly refers to additional ablations in its missing appendix, preventing a reliable assessment of how much supplementary analysis was added.

E5.justification: v3 Table S reports means and standard deviations over three experiments using different randomized decay matrices. No equivalent uncertainty reporting appears in v1's supplied main text, but its supplementary ablations are unavailable. Therefore, first introduction of this reporting practice cannot be established. Neither PDF establishes increased repeated-run counts for the shared benchmark results.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–6 retain their scores. v3 substantially extends the reported outcomes, including SD3-medium FID of 12.24 for QVGen versus 13.82 for Q-DM (Table T), SVG combination latencies, additional fidelity metrics and supplementary analyses. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions. Table L's attribution and Figure 6(c)'s 1.3B speedup calculation contain inconsistencies.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 becomes Theorem 3.1 and revises the regret bound: the diameter factor is squared, and minimum/maximum coordinate learning rates replace the single learning-rate factors. This refines the same convex regret argument. Appendix C supplies a derivation, but comparison with v1's promised proof is impossible because that appendix is absent.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the first-video-QAT positioning, gradient-norm motivation, auxiliary modules, overhead-free rank decay, full-precision-comparable 4-bit quality and effective 3-bit quantization. The headline improvements of 25.28 in Dynamic Degree and 8.43 in Scene Consistency are unchanged. Additional experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: The central convergence interpretation remains. v3 adds explicit compatibility with sparse attention, a Pareto-frontier interpretation, and qualifications that image transfer is preliminary and large gains may depend on video-specific observations. Its Pareto example is overstated: Table 1's 3-bit CogVideoX aesthetic score of 50.54 remains below 4-bit LSQ's 54.20.

D1.justification: v3 B, D and F supply pseudocode, samplers, learning rates, batch sizes, preprocessing, distributed-training choices, baseline layer exceptions and GPU-day costs. New image-study details are also reported. However, v1 explicitly places detailed setups in its missing appendix, so the extent of new reproducibility disclosures for retained experiments cannot be reliably determined.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting references for image experiments, metrics and implementation, including SD3, LAION-5B, UniMatch, GPTQ and FlashAttention. References such as BRECQ, LTX-Video, QBitOpt and incremental network quantization disappear. The principal research positioning remains, while SVG gains an explicit complementarity discussion. Moving the video-model review to Appendix A is not removal.

P1.justification: Most abstract, introduction, method and main experimental prose is retained. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, with the video-model discussion moved to Appendix A. v3 adds appendix navigation and specific cross-references, shortens several ablation labels, and makes limited wording edits rather than extensively rewriting the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template and repositions existing displays, removes red performance-gap subscripts from the main tables, and adds Figure 6(c). Its appendix supplies Algorithm 1, Tables G–T and qualitative Figures A–H, including expanded displays of existing ablations. This substantially expands and reorganizes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 is more self-contained and supplies useful-looking implementation, image-generation and supplementary evidence. However, Table L's purported CogVideoX-5B results reproduce Wan1.3B decay-ablation values and conflict with Table 2. Figure 6(c) also reports a 1.70-fold speedup although 4.02/2.53 is approximately 1.59. These unresolved reliability problems, together with v1's unavailable appendix, prevent a confident assessment of the net quality improvement.
